items.stem: A Markov chain has states 0,1,2,3, initial distribution (1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4), and transition matrix P=[[.25,.25,.25,.25],[0,.50,.50,0],[.75,0,.25,0],[.25,.50,0,.25]]. Which statements are correct?
items.explanation: State 0 has a self-loop with positive probability, so its period is one; irreducibility then makes every state aperiodic. The transition graph allows every state to reach every other state, so the chain is irreducible. By the Markov property, P(X₃=2|X₂=1,X₁=1,X₀=2)=p₁₂=0.5. Finally, X₀ is uniform on {0,1,2,3}, so E(X₀)=(0+1+2+3)/4=3/2. All four statements are true.

A.why: State 0 has a self-loop, and irreducibility transfers period one to every state.

B.why: Every state communicates with every other through positive-probability paths.

C.why: The Markov property reduces the probability to the matrix entry p₁₂=0.5.

D.why: The initial distribution is uniform, giving mean 3/2.

items.stem: Consider the three-state Markov chain with transition matrix P=[[1/2,1/4,1/4],[1/3,0,2/3],[1/2,1/2,0]]. Which statements are correct?
statements: The chain has a unique stationary distribution.
items.explanation: Every state communicates with every other state, so the chain is irreducible. State 1 has a self-loop with probability 1/2, so its period is one. In an irreducible chain all states have the same period; hence state 2 also has period one. A finite irreducible Markov chain has a unique stationary distribution. Therefore A, C and D are true.

A.why: Irreducibility transfers the period-one property from state 1, which has a self-loop.

B.why: The chain is irreducible and contains a self-loop, so its period is one.

C.why: All states communicate through positive-probability paths.

D.why: Every finite irreducible Markov chain has a unique stationary distribution.

items.stem: A Markov chain has transition matrix P=[[1/2,1/3,1/6],[3/4,0,1/4],[0,1,0]]. Which statements are correct?
statements: The two-step return probability p₁₁^(2) is 1/6.
items.explanation: Every state can reach every other state: from state 1 we can reach 2 or 3, from state 2 we can reach 1 or 3, and from state 3 we move to state 2. Thus the chain is irreducible. State 1 has a self-loop with probability 1/2, so its period is one; irreducibility gives period one for every state. The two-step return probability is p₁₁^(2)=P₁₁P₁₁+P₁₂P₂₁+P₁₃P₃₁=1/4+1/4+0=1/2, not 1/6. Solving πP=π gives π=(1/2,1/3,1/6). Hence A and D are true.

A.why: All three states communicate, so the chain is irreducible.

B.why: A positive self-loop at state 1 makes the period one.

D.why: The vector (1/2,1/3,1/6) satisfies πP=π and sums to one.

items.stem: Cars arrive according to a Poisson process at rate 10 per hour. Each car independently picks up a passenger with probability 1/10. You are second in line. What is the probability that you wait more than 2 hours for a pickup?
items.explanation: Thinning a Poisson process by independently retaining each arrival with probability 1/10 gives a Poisson process of passenger pickups with rate 10×(1/10)=1 per hour. Since you are second in line, your waiting time is the time until the second event of a rate-1 Poisson process. Equivalently, the number of pickups in 2 hours is Poisson with mean 2. You wait more than 2 hours exactly when there are fewer than two pickups: P(N(2)≤1)=P(N=0)+P(N=1)=e^(−2)+2e^(−2)=3e^(−2). Option C is correct.

items.stem: Let (Yₙ, Fₙ) be a martingale. Which identity is true for n,m≥0?
items.explanation: A martingale is adapted and integrable and satisfies the defining conditional-expectation property E(Yₖ|Fⱼ)=Yⱼ whenever j≤k. Taking k=n+m and j=n gives E(Yₙ₊ₘ|Fₙ)=Yₙ. This says that, given the information available at time n, the best conditional expectation of a future martingale value is its current value.
